children: By George Glover, Mariapaula Gonzalez, and Kit Norton

Stocks rose Tuesday as investor excitement around Anthropic's initial public offering continued to boost chip and artificial-intelligence infrastructure stocks. Wall Street, against this backdrop, awaited several Big Tech earnings and the Federal Reserve's decision on interest rates.

Nvidia rose 1.4%. The chip maker said it would invest $3 billion in Meta Platforms' recently announced share offer. In exchange, Meta will expand its deployment of Nvidia hardware to support its artificial-intelligence agents. Shares of Meta fell 0.7%.

Broadcom gained 3.9% to $342.10. D.A. Davidson analyst Gil Luria raised his rating on Broadcom stock to Buy from Neutral and boosted his price target to $400 from $350. The decision to upgrade Broadcom came as Anthropic's IPO filing confirmed the scale and details of the partnership between the two companies.
Among other AI-adjacent stocks, Dell Technologies advanced 8.1% and Bloom Energy rose 8.2%, adding to a 5.5% gain from the previous session.

United Parcel Service rose 3%. The company surpassed Wall Street's estimates for the third quarter and boosted its guidance. UPS now expects 2026 revenue of $92.6 billion — up from prior guidance of $91.2 billion.

General Motors gained 6.3%. The Detroit-based car maker announced it was transferring its stock listing to the Nasdaq exchange from the New York Stock Exchange It will keep its "GM" ticker symbol and can benefit from things such as indexation and lower listing fees. The change is effective on Nov. 17.

Boeing dropped 9.6%. The aerospace company posted an earnings miss, but its free cash flow of $464 million topped analysts' $238 million projection. Beyond the numbers, investors will be looking for an update on plane production and when the new 777 will be certified for commercial service.

JetBlue gained 29%. The airline raised its full-year forecast for revenue per available seat mile growth to 13.5% to 14.5%, from 10% to 12.5% previously. Still, it posted a wider-than-expected loss as soaring fuel prices continued to weigh on its profit.

Corning declined 0.4%. Though the optical networking company posted an earnings beat and offered solid quarterly guidance, it wasn't enough to quell investor concerns about the massive amount of spending needed for the AI buildout. Fellow optical networking stocks Lumentum and Coherent rose 7.7% and 6.4%, respectively.

SoFi Technologies climbed 15%. The digital neobank raised its full-year 2026 guidance and projects adjusted net revenue of about $5.04 billion. The rise in share price broke Sofi out of the post-earnings slump it has endured since last October.

Royal Caribbean advanced 7.4% as the cruise ship operator beat third-quarter earnings expectations and raised its full-year guidance, signaling to investors that the run-up in fuel costs hasn't had much of an impact on its business.
Celestica advanced 12%. The electronics manufacturer posted strong third-quarter results and raised its full-year outlook, citing the boom in demand for artificial-intelligence infrastructure.
Nucor gained 6.3%. The steel producer's third-quarter profit surged, with earnings for its steel mills segment more than doubling from a year ago.
The S&P 500 was a tale of two water solutions companies at each extreme.

Pentair rose 13% and was the best-performing component in the index for the trading session. The company posted better-than-expected earnings and revised higher its full-year revenue outlook based on the acquisition to boost its data-center business exposure.
Xylem, another water solutions company, dropped 12% and was the worst-performing S&P 500 component after the company missed third-quarter earnings estimates and cut its full-year guidance.
